title: Ready for Action
description: A bush viper (Atheris hispida) coils up on a tree branch in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The snakes are highly venomous and native to sub-Saharan Africa. Though more than 30,000 people in the region die from venomous snakebites each year, it is believed that the number may be double due to unrecorded deaths, as National Geographic reported in December 2020.
translated_description: 在刚果民主共和国，一条灌木蝰蛇（学名：Atheris hispida）盘绕在树枝上。这种蛇毒性极强，原产于撒哈拉以南非洲地区。尽管该地区每年有超过3万人因毒蛇咬伤致死，但据《国家地理》2020年12月报道，由于存在未记录的死亡案例，实际死亡人数可能翻倍。
